title: The API that changed under our feet
text:
Our mobile app broke on a Monday morning, and for an hour nobody understood why. The backend had not been deployed over the weekend, the logs looked clean, and yet thousands of users saw an empty screen.

The cause turned out to be a third-party payment provider. Without any announcement, they had renamed one field in their response from "amount" to "total". Our code assumed the old name, so it quietly read an empty value and passed it further down the chain. Nothing crashed, which made the bug even harder to spot.

The fix took five minutes. The real work started afterwards. We added validation for every external response, so that unexpected data fails loudly instead of silently. We also wrote contract tests that run against the provider's sandbox every night, and we subscribed to their changelog, which, embarrassingly, nobody had done before.

The lesson is uncomfortable but useful: an integration is a relationship, and the other side is free to change without asking you. Treat every external API as unreliable, even a famous one. Be strict about what you accept, log what you reject, and never assume that a quiet system is a healthy one.

questions.prompt: What caused the problem in the app?
options: A payment provider changed a field name without warning
A server ran out of memory
questions.explanation: Провайдер перейменував поле з amount на total без оголошення, а код очікував стару назву.

questions.prompt: Why was the bug hard to find?
options: Nothing crashed and the logs looked clean.
The code was written in an unknown language.
questions.explanation: Помилки не було видно: код тихо прочитав порожнє значення й працював далі.

options: Treat external APIs as unreliable and validate what they return
Fix bugs only after users complain
questions.explanation: Автор радить ставитися до зовнішніх API як до ненадійних і перевіряти кожну відповідь.
